title: introduce-workload-hint-profiles-probe-and-safe-fallbacks
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: many customers run into conservative defaults for batching/caching/quantization that leave money on the table because conservative heuristics can't adapt to unusual request shapes (short tail latency-sensitive or long-tail streaming). This PR adds a lightweight probe-run mode and 'hint profile' generator that derives conservative suggested batching/cache/quant presets from short, non-invasive workload probes and model shape telemetry. The hint profiles are intended as prescriptive defaults for Redwood Optimize and Dedicated autoscaling hooks but are conservative by design and include automatic safety fallbacks. What this changes: 1) runtime: a probe mode that executes short-duration synthetic traffic (configurable sample rate and duration) and collects sequence length distribution, cold KV frequency, and per-step latency histograms; 2) hint generator: heuristics that synthesize batching window, target microbatch size, prefix cache TTL, and recommended quant profile (fp16/4bit-opti) with an attached risk score and fallback multiplier; 3) CLI/API: a new econ-prober CLI and an admin API route to request hint profiles for a given model/route; 4) console docs and a short runbook for safe rollout; 5) tests and telemetry to ensure probes do not perturb production SLOs. Safety model: profiles include a "safety_multiplier" (default 0.75) that is applied before any automatic rollout; when applied to Dedicated pools the platform will only use the hint if live SLO/latency checks remain green for a configurable observation window. Checklist: [x] probe runtime implemented and gated behind feature flag [x] hint synthesis heuristics and risk scoring [x] admin API and CLI added [x] unit + integration tests [x] docs and runbook added [x] e2e smoke test in perf-canary. Related: ENG-4018 (probe infra setup), PM-2087 (product spec). Rollout plan: merge behind feature flag, run opt-in for internal clusters for two weeks, collect regressions and tune safety_multiplier, then enable opt-out rollout for early customers. CI: all pipeline stages pass; perf canary scheduled post-merge. No breaking API changes.
commits: feat(probe): add lightweight runtime probe mode with sampling and telemetry hooks
feat(hint): synthesize hint profiles from probe telemetry and export as YAML
chore(docs): add runbook and CLI usage examples for econ-prober
review_thread: Caleb Rivera: Can you add a guard so probes don't run during peak windows? Author: Probes are disabled by default and respect cluster maintenance windows and peak schedules; added explicit guard in runtime/probe/probe_runner.go

Marta Nguyen: The risk scoring looks heuristic-heavy; any plan to back off automatically on noisy signals? Author: Added a conservative noise detector and an early-exit path when variance exceeds threshold; we also persist the last safe profile to revert to
Ravi Singh: Please ensure the CLI requires admin scope and audit logs. Author: CLI and API calls now require org.admin scope and log to audit.events; added test for audit entry
Caleb Rivera: LGTM after small nits. Marta Nguyen: Approved. Ravi Singh: Approved.
release_notes: Adds a probe-based hint profile generator to suggest conservative batching/caching/quant defaults for models. The feature is behind a feature flag and includes safety multipliers and automatic fallbacks. Intended to reduce unit economics waste while preventing regressions.
notes: This PR purposefully targets conservative defaults only; we intentionally do not enable automatic aggressive rollouts without manual opt-in. Perf-canary job will run for 48h after merge to validate no regression on internal traffic.
tests_summary: Added unit coverage for hint scoring heuristics and an integration test that runs a short probe against a local runtime instance and validates produced YAML profile format and safety fields.
